output.answer: Arini Capital presented a European-credit investment proposal centered on a $200 million Master Custody Account. The proposed allocation was $50 million to the Arini Credit Master Fund, an open-ended all-weather long/short credit strategy; $75 million to the Arini Credit Opportunities Fund, a catalyst-driven public/private strategy focused on restructurings, refinancings and capital solutions; and $75 million to bespoke direct investments, expected mainly to be private European opportunities. Arini also explained its sector-specialist, fundamentally driven research process and its ability to express credit views through bonds, loans, structured products and new-capital solutions; SBCERA subsequently approved the account on September 4, 2025, subject to due diligence and legal documentation.

key_facts.fact: SBCERA's Board approved establishing a Master Custody Account with Arini Capital Management, with a $200 million initial allocation, on September 4, 2025, subject to due diligence and legal documentation.
The proposed allocation was $50 million to the Arini Credit Master Fund, $75 million to the Arini Credit Opportunities Fund, and $75 million to direct investments.
The Credit Master Fund was described as an open-ended all-weather long/short credit strategy emphasizing public bonds, loans, CDS and structured credit, primarily in Europe.
The Credit Opportunities Fund was described as a drawdown hybrid strategy focused on catalyst-driven restructurings, refinancings and capital solutions, with a 50/50 public-private profile.
In the presentation, Arini described a sector-specialist research model that continuously tracks companies and can express views through bonds, loans, new capital solutions and structured products.
